{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Subject:** Playbook review of the Vendor's draft Master Services Agreement  
**Findings reviewed:** 18 rules | 6 deviations, 1 missing, 11 compliant

---

## 1. Executive summary

The draft is materially acceptable on the terms that matter most to us. The core risk-allocation provisions — Vendor IP and data indemnities (§ 20), ownership of Customer Data and Deliverables (§ 14), the mutual liability cap and Excluded Claims (§ 21), licence scope including Affiliates and contractors (§ 13), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), warranties (§ 19), insurance (§ 18), governing law (§ 28) and assignment/change-of-control (§ 24) — all meet our preferred positions and require no redline.

Our concerns are concentrated in a cluster of Customer-side obligations that sit outside the playbook, several of which are walk-away items: a full-term exclusivity commitment (§ 2.2), a USD 25,000 per-day liquidated damages penalty on us (§ 7.6), an open-ended MFN running against us (§ 7.2), and an unlimited, no-notice audit right with remote access to our systems (§ 22.1). Notably, three of these contradict § 12.3, in which Vendor expressly acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment — so the redlines largely conform the document to its own stated bargain.

We also address a one-way 18-month no-hire (§ 12.4), a 180-day non-renewal notice window (§ 8.2) and the absence of any Customer termination-for-convenience right under a three-year term (§ 8.1, § 9).

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 (with 20.2–20.5, 21.3) | Preferred position met; IP indemnity extends to Affiliates and indemnities sit outside the cap as Excluded Claims. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 (with 14.2–14.4, 15.1) | We retain Customer Data and pre-existing IP; Deliverables assigned to us; no model training without consent. Ownership is conditioned on payment of Fees — noted, not flagged. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with 21.3, 18.2) | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with full Excluded Claims set. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with 24.2, 24.4, 13.3) | Free Affiliate/successor assignment for us; Vendor assignment needs our consent; no repricing on our change of control. |
| 5 | **High** | **EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer** | **Deviation** | **§ 2.2** | Full-term sole-and-exclusive provider obligation with no performance exit; walk-away territory and contradicts §§ 2.1 and 12.3. |
| 6 | **High** | **LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer** | **Deviation** | **§ 7.6** | USD 25,000 per day for any dependency delay, uncapped; walk-away territory. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with 13.2–13.4) | Worldwide grant covering Affiliates and contractors; perpetual paid-up licence to delivered material; narrow restrictions. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction; § 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to build, buy and compete. Conflicts with §§ 2.2 and 7.2 are handled under those rules. |
| 9 | **High** | **T4C — Termination for convenience** | **Missing** | **§ 9 (see § 9.5); term at § 8.1** | Only for-cause, insolvency and force-majeure exits exist; no Customer convenience right under a three-year term. Favourably, Vendor has none either. |
| 10 | **Medium** | **AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer** | **Deviation** | **§ 22.1** | Audits at any time without notice plus remote system access; walk-away territory and contradicts § 22.2. Cost allocation in § 22.2 already meets our position. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 (with 28.3) | New York law, exclusive New York County jurisdiction, no arbitration; escalation preserves urgent relief. |
| 12 | **Medium** | **MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer** | **Deviation** | **§ 7.2** | Open-ended obligation to give Vendor our best supplier terms; walk-away territory and inconsistent with § 12.3. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2.1 (with 7.1, 12.3) | No minimum quantity, take-or-pay or minimum-use charges; declining to order is not a shortfall. |
| 14 | **Medium** | **NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer** | **Deviation** | **§ 12.4** | One-way, 18 months post-termination, covers any Vendor employee at any time during the term, bars engagement, no general-advertising carve-out. |
| 15 | **Medium** | **RENEWAL — Auto-renewal notice window** | **Deviation** | **§ 8.2** | 180-day non-renewal notice exceeds our 90-day walk-away threshold and fails the 60-day fallback. Uplift cap in § 8.3 (CPI/3%) is favourable. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 (with 11.2–11.3) | Six months' assistance at expiring rates; 30-day data return with no fee-dispute hostage; deletion only after we confirm return. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with 19.2–19.5) | Workmanlike performance, conformance warranties, non-exclusive remedies; disclaimer does not limit express warranties. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with 18.2) | All limits met (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' comp) for term plus one year. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These four provisions are identified in our findings as walk-away territory. We should not sign without resolution.

1. **§ 2.2 — Customer exclusivity.** Full-term exclusive dealing with no performance-based exit. **Position:** delete. **Fallback:** a defined-category, 12-month exclusivity that terminates on service-level failure.
2. **§ 7.6 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** USD 25,000 per day for any dependency delay, however minor, with no cap. **Position:** delete; Vendor retains schedule relief and may recover demonstrable standby costs.
3. **§ 7.2 — Customer-side MFN.** Open-ended obligation to extend Vendor the best terms we give any other technology supplier. **Position:** delete. MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.
4. **§ 22.1 — Unlimited audit with system access.** Audits at any time without notice, with remote access to our systems. **Position:** limit to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, in business hours, via an independent auditor bound by confidentiality; delete system access.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven open items:
   - Delete Customer exclusivity (§ 2.2).
   - Delete Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.6).
   - Delete Customer-side MFN (§ 7.2).
   - Limit audit frequency and notice and delete system access (§ 22.1).
   - Narrow the non-solicit to mutual, 12 months, personnel involved in the Services, with standard carve-outs (§ 12.4).
   - Shorten the non-renewal notice window to 30 days (§ 8.2).
   - Insert a new § 9.6: Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and confirm Vendor has no convenience right.
2. **Frame §§ 2.2, 7.2 and 12.4 as internal-consistency fixes.** Vendor already acknowledges in § 12.3 that we have made no exclusivity, MFN or no-hire commitment; the redline conforms the operative clauses to that acknowledgement.
3. **Escalate to the business only if Vendor resists the walk-away items.** For § 2.2 we can offer the defined-category, 12-month, SLA-conditioned fallback; on §§ 7.6, 7.2 and 22.1 we have no fallback short of the positions above.
4. **Confirm no further changes to compliant clauses.** Sections 11, 13, 14, 18, 19, 20, 21, 24 and 28 should be marked "no comment" so negotiation stays focused and we do not reopen favourable terms.
5. **Note for the record (no action):** ownership under § 14 is conditioned on payment of Fees, and § 8.3 lacks nothing material given the CPI/3% uplift cap — both noted in the rationale rather than redlined."}
